_comment: Fetch layers for running TESSERA v2 inference ourselves (no v2 product is
published; see docs/TesseraV2Inference.md). Every acquisition in the
window's time range, one item group per scene, chronological -- the
d-pixel inputs their pipeline builds with its bash + Rust preprocessing.
Copied from config_pastis_rslearn.json, which is where they were first
written and which declares them inline; a unit test holds the two
identical EXCEPT for sentinel2_l2a_all's max_matches (150 there, 300
here).
MAX_MATCHES, measured 2026-08-06. The layers sort datetime ASCENDING, so
hitting the cap drops the END of the year -- a seasonal loss, not random
attrition. At S2=150 (the pastis value) 4.94% of ethiopia_crops windows
were truncated; at 300 that is 0.32% (ethiopia) / 0.35% (africa), and S1
at 100 truncates 0.23-0.35% of africa windows (zero on ethiopia, which
has no ascending coverage at all in MPC's RTC archive). That residual was
accepted rather than raising again. Ceiling for any future raise: the v2
student bins valid observations at 256 (tessera_v2_infer.BIN_EDGES), so
scenes beyond roughly 500-600 cannot reach the model.
B01/B09 (60 m, stored at 40 m) are NOT used by TESSERA v2 inference, which
reads only the first two band sets via S2_BAND_SETS/TESSERA_S2_INDICES.
They are here for pixel_mosaic_export.py, whose composite has to be a full
12-band S2 input to stay comparable with the year-aligned mo layers. They
are deliberately absent from config_pastis_rslearn.json, so the drift test
exempts them.
This is NOT a dataset config on its own. tessera_v2_export.py
write_fetch_config merges these layers with a dataset's storage/tile_store
blocks into a config passed via `rslearn dataset prepare --config`, so
they never enter the dataset's own config.json -- these layers are
EXPENSIVE (a year of scenes per window), and a run that forgot
--enabled-layers against a config carrying them would fetch a year of
imagery for every eval window. Always pair them with --group <fetch
group>.
